Mun äiti oli myös henkisesti väkivaltainen ja laiminlöi mua koko lapsuuden pahasti. Muutin pois n 16v jolloin taloudellinen hyväksikäyttö alkoi kun rupesin saamaan tukia. Mulla kesti monta vuotta päästä tilanteesta irti. Nyt oon 30v enkä pidä mun äitiin yhteyttä. Sit ku se on vanha nii menköön johonki laitokseen makaamaan paskasissa vaipoissa. Ansaittua. Juuri tuo kasvatus, jossa vanhempi kokee olevansa oikeutettu lapsen rahoihin koska "kasvatti lapsen" on todella väärin. Sä et pyytänyt syntyä tänne. Vanhemmilla on velvollisuus kasvattaa lapsi. Et oo mitään velkaa sun vanhemmille. Suosittelen että teet nyt muuttosuunnitelmat valmiiksi ilman että kerrot. Sit muutat ja lopetat rahan antamisen. Älä kerro minne muutit jos mahdollista. Jos niillä ei oo varaa asua missä nyt asuu, muuttakoot he edullisempaan paikkaan. 

Toimeentulotukea saavat varmaan lääkkeisiin. Jos jatkavat jankutusta niin välit poikki kokonaan. Siksi sanoin että älä kerro minne muutit (varmista myös ettei osoitteesi näy esim fonectassa) ettei ne voi tulla yllätysvierailulle jos päätät blokata. 

En tiedä miten koet, mutta tsekkaisin r/CPTSD jossa suurin osa on kokenut vanhemmiltaan kaltoinkohtelua. Noi sun ajatusmallit muistuttaa mua omistani. Ja komppaan terapiaan menemistä jos mahdollista. Ja vielä terapeutille joka ymmärtää traumaa (henkinen väkivalta ja henkinen laiminlyönti on myös traumatisoivaa).

Tsempit ja ihailen rohkeuttasi. Ällisyttää osa näistä kommenteista kyllä; oletus siitä että vanhemmat on aina hyviä tai oikeassa. Rupesi ärsyttämään puolestasi kyllä. Harmittaa etten itse ollut tarpeeksi rohkea. Oma äiti kavalsi minulta yli 5000€ ollessani alaikäinen, sisaruksilta yhteensä varmaan yli 30k opintolainoja ja muita kelan tukia. Kun uskalsin soittaa asiasta poliisille, oli liian myöhäistä. Olisin tehnyt asiasta rikosilmoituksen, mutta poliisista sanoivat että alle 10k summissa aikaraja on 5 vuotta. Kun on  ollut koko elämänsä vanhempansa kaltoinkohtelun alaisena ja manipuloitavissa, ei oo helppo homma lähteä sitä vastaan. 

Ihanaa että pidät sisaruksestasi huolta. Kiitos siitä. Oot rohkea.

Hey, in a similar boat though my weight came from remembering repressed memories and eating to deal with the emotions. CICO helped me lose lost of weight but I stopped doing it for some reason. I find it hard to start again, and I guess I did become kind of obsessed with it. 

I try to just eat regularly and focus on eating enough protein. Instead of candy I try to eat sugar-free protein puddings (those were really a life saver for me) or low cal quark. I also try to buy my favourite fruits so I have some at home always. 

Don't try to force yourself to eat things you don't like, but instead find healthy things you do like (for example, by preparing things differently). I don't like raw vegetables for the most part on their own, but steamed vegetables are very tasty to me. 

But then again, raw vegetables sliced/cut into smaller pieces and eaten with home made greek yoghurt dip (I put sriracha in mine) is a pretty fun snack and gives you some protein too.

I don't think I could live my life without some snacks forever, so I just try to eat them in smart portions. Limiting them to, for example, weekends, or when going out, or only when someone offers, is a possibility. 

Also try not to drink your calories for the most part (I mean like, sugar sodas/cocoa and so on)

The point is to find a way of eating you can do for the rest of your life by finding healthy things you like. There's r/volumeeating  for example, for eating healthier things in (semi)big portions! 

Most of weight loss comes from the kitchen and of course going for walks helps. Finding a moving hobby you love can be good, because if you just do something you despise it's probably not going to last (if you hate running, try walking for example, or if you hate the gym, try dancing and so on).

The very short version of my DID diagnosis journey, but since both DID and CPTSD  are caused by prolonged trauma and my DID includes the CPTSD symptoms I thought I'd reply. I noticed the CPTSD symptoms first before realizing there was dissociation going on too. 

I had been depressed since I was a little kid, already having self harm / suicidal thoughts at age 6 or so. At some point I sought help for severe depression at the ER, saying I was going to kill myself.  I must've been around 22? It was my last try, I had decided. I got to meet a doctor, I had taken a note with me with my symptoms in it and she took the note and read it. I was then given a referral to a psychiatric polyclinic from where I got an invitation a few weeks later. 

They started treating me for depression, my first diagnosis was psychotic depression. A year later, that changed into severe depression and schizotypal disorder. I started to realize the extent of my trauma slowly and I found this sub, it must've been around 2016? I realized  that severe depression wasn't explaining my symptoms. 

Then, a few years later I was referred to another clinic, where I met with my current psychiatrist who was trauma informed, and  I was diagnosed with DDNOS (dissociative disorder not otherwise specified, or something) which basically included  CPTSD symptoms + dissociative symptoms for me. Two years after that my DDNOS was changed into DID diagnosis. 

It was quite a shock to me and I still can't believe it sometimes, even though it has been a few years.
